name: Railways (RRB)
description: Indian Railways awareness for RRB NTPC and Group D exams.

questions.question: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 between which stations?
questions.explanation: The first train covered ~34 km from Bombay's Bori Bunder to Thane with 14 carriages and 400 passengers.

questions.question: Indian Railways operates under which Union ministry?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Railways (Railway Board at its apex) runs Indian Railways, one of the world's largest employers.

questions.question: What is the width of Indian Railways' broad gauge?
questions.explanation: Broad gauge (1,676 mm) carries the bulk of traffic; metre gauge is 1,000 mm and narrow gauge is 762 mm.

questions.question: Vande Bharat Express, India's first indigenous semi-high-speed train, runs at a maximum operational speed of:
questions.explanation: Vande Bharat trains run at up to 160 km/h (designed for 180); the first ran between Delhi and Varanasi in 2019.

questions.question: How many zones does Indian Railways have (after the creation of South Coast Railway)?
questions.explanation: South Coast Railway (headquartered at Visakhapatnam) became the 18th zone in 2019.

questions.question: The Konkan Railway line passes through which states?
options: Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: The 741-km Konkan Railway runs from Roha (Maharashtra) to Thokur/Mangaluru (Karnataka) via Goa.

questions.question: The National Academy of Indian Railways, which trains railway officers, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: NAIR (formerly Railway Staff College) in Vadodara trains Indian Railway service officers.

questions.question: India's first metro rail system, opened in 1984, was in which city?
questions.explanation: Kolkata Metro (Esplanade–Bhowanipore stretch, 24 October 1984) was India's first metro.

questions.question: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor connects Dadri (UP) to which port?
questions.explanation: The Western DFC runs Dadri–JNPT (Mumbai); the Eastern DFC connects Ludhiana to Dankuni (near Kolkata).

questions.question: RPF stands for what?
questions.explanation: The RPF safeguards railway property and passenger areas; law and order on trains falls to the GRP (Government Railway Police).

questions.question: Which is the highest railway station in India?
questions.explanation: Ghum (2,258 m) on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is India's highest station — a UNESCO World Heritage line.

questions.question: Which three mountain railways of India are jointly a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
options: Darjeeling Himalayan, Nilgiri Mountain and Kalka–Shimla
Darjeeling Himalayan, Kangra Valley and Matheran
questions.explanation: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (1881), Nilgiri Mountain Railway (1908) and Kalka–Shimla Railway (1903) form the UNESCO 'Mountain Railways of India'.

questions.question: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in which year, ending a 92-year-old practice?
questions.explanation: Following the Bibek Debroy committee's recommendation, the railway budget was merged into the Union Budget from 2017–18.

questions.question: KAVACH is Indian Railways' indigenous system for what?
questions.explanation: KAVACH is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system that brakes automatically to prevent collisions and signal overshoots.

questions.question: Which is the fastest train in India by maximum operating speed (as of 2025–26)?
questions.explanation: Vande Bharat trains are India's fastest regular services; Gatimaan (160 km/h) briefly shared the mark before Vande Bharat's wider rollout.
